semantic_notes: The single-run correctness theorem combines key sortedness and payload permutation under LinearOrder keys and the actual runsOn length<=1 premise. Its empty and singleton executions cost2 and4 respectively, retaining scan and dispatch.

Ascending and descending chain premises establish at most one run, including empty inputs. Exact execution formulas separately retain n>=2 for ascending cost6*n-4 and nonempty for descending cost3*n+1.

Key-sorted and strictly descending specializations preserve their intended assumptions: LinearOrder for sorted-key reasoning, only LT/DecidableLT and the explicit Pairwise descending premise for operational reversal.
The Empty payload example compiles an eliminator comparator without introducing an inhabitant. Generic singleton examples remain law-free in arbitrary payload/comparator.
The concrete two/three-element ascending scan costs7/13 and full execution costs8/14; descending scan costs6/9 and execution7/10. The ascending ties input[1,1,2,3] is retained as one run at cost19.

The ties execution costs20. Boundary and restart examples retain actual worker and scanner outputs/costs: [3,1,2] gives[[1,3],[2]] at10; [1,3,2,4] gives[[1,3],[2,4]] at15; the odd-run extension[1,3,2,4,0] gives three runs at19.

Tagged weak descent[(3,A),(3,B),(2,C)] produces the stable tied ascending run followed by the singleton, cost11. Explicit negated length<=1 conclusions prevent applying the zero/single-run dispatcher to this or the other multiple-run cases.

Arbitrary builder restart returns the represented prefix and new run at14; a deliberately unsorted builder yields[2,1,3] at6 and is explicitly not KeySorted. Worker correctness is not overgeneralized to arbitrary unsorted accumulators.

The arbitrary descending accumulator base returns a::acc at3 without an unstated sortedness premise. A reversing callback with uniform cost k still satisfies the cost bound without Rep; the concrete continuation returns[3,2] at26.

Capturing composition is cost1 while evaluating the captured callbacks in the worker costs p+q+4, so capture cost is not confused with application cost. Both empty outer runs and singleton empty inner run dispatch to[] at1 and equal tick of the corresponding existing allRun.
